# Place, Route, and Timing with nextpnr

## Concepts

Placement assigns physical sites; routing connects them through the FPGA's programmable interconnect. Timing closure means the implementation meets its specified timing checks. A successful bitstream build without adequate constraints does not establish correct timing.

Constraint coverage includes clocks, generated clocks, external interface timing, pin assignments, and IO standards. False-path and multicycle exceptions require a design justification; they must not conceal paths that need to meet the ordinary clock requirement.

## Implementation

Select a nextpnr backend and device supported by the installed toolchain. An Artix-7 implementation requires a compatible toolchain and a board-specific pin map. Record the board, device, backend, architecture data, and bitstream tools before selecting commands.

For each critical path, identify launch and capture registers, combinational logic, routing contribution, and slack. A UART's slow serial rate does not relax its synchronous counters and state machines: a 50 MHz implementation still has a 20 ns system-clock target.

Compare pre-route and post-route reports. Placement and routing can expose long control nets or congested paths that are absent from an RTL-level view.

## Hands-on Experiments

Implement a verified small block on the selected FPGA. Record utilization, requested clock period, worst timing result, and unconstrained paths. Change one RTL or placement variable at a time and compare reports under the same constraints.

Inventory asynchronous inputs and clock crossings. Document which synchronizers or protocols handle each crossing and why each timing exception is valid. Keep the board pin map with the experiment.
